By arranging laser-trapped atoms into a quantum simulator, they recreated two different quantum tipping points and watched the atoms fall into the exact energy ratios predicted by theory. The

items.title: Wildlife tracking to fill gaps in monarch migration research
items.summary: Every fall, monarch butterflies fuel up on nectar from Iowa's fall-blooming wildflowers before embarking on an extraordinary migration from North America to Mexico. But the pathways they take and how their travel is affected by weather and other factors have largely remained a mystery.

items.title: This common mistake can add nearly 7 points to your blood pressure reading
items.summary: A common mistake during blood pressure checks could make readings appear substantially higher than they really are. Johns Hopkins researchers found that leaving the arm unsupported can raise systolic readings by about 6.5 mmHg, potentially affecting a hypertension diagnosis.

items.title: Celebrity Traitors: Research suggests that some contestants will find the game tougher than it looks
items.summary: "The Traitors" has become essential viewing for millions of fans. The TV game show, in which a group of "faithfuls" try to identify a smaller number of hidden traitors, is all about truth and lies.

items.title: Fine-tuning cobalt for cleaner chemical transformations
items.summary: Finding alternatives to precious metals in chemical manufacturing may be less like sourcing a substitute and more like tuning an instrument already in hand.

items.title: Bacteria can make plant-based foods healthier for humans and animals
items.summary: New research from the DTU National Food Institute and Aarhus University shows that microorganisms can be used to specifically alter the amino acid composition of plant-based foods, making them more nutritious and therefore healthier.

items.title: Why some Ukrainian refugees struggle to rebuild their careers after arriving in Canada
items.summary: The Russian invasion of Ukraine continues into 2026, with millions of Ukrainians displaced around the world. Many arrived in host countries with professional experience, degrees and specialized skills. Yet displacement often leaves highly educated refugees unable to continue their previous careers.

items.title: Scientists develop 'floating scarecrow' to protect threatened seabirds
items.summary: New research has shown that a "floating scarecrow" developed by U.K.-based scientists and a repurposed bird-scaring kite can help save threatened seabirds from getting caught in fishing nets.

items.title: Community-led archaeology project uncovers a major monastery of medieval Scotland
items.summary: Community-led archaeology has uncovered the remains of an early medieval monastery in Argyll, western Scotland, identifying it as the high-ranking ecclesiastical center of Lios Mòr, previously known only from historical references and local traditions.

items.title: Devastating year for Switzerland's glaciers after extreme heat and low snow
items.summary: Switzerland's glaciers lost more than 5% of their ice volume in 2026. Although melt rates did not quite reach the record levels of 2022, glacier thickness decreased by an average of 2.5 to 4 meters (8 to 13 feet) this year, and some glacier tongues lost up to 10 meters (33 feet) of ice. items.title: Confronting demons: How acoustic and AI technology brought ancient Etruscan tombs back to life
items.summary: Although it is not always obvious, sound guides how we experience the world around us. And the latest archaeoacoustic techniques show that even the world's earliest architects understood this.

items.title: Key protein for cells' gene regulation needs a chaperone to do its job
items.summary: A protein that's essential to every cell's ability to turn off unnecessary genes is well known for its key function of compacting genes and its connection to cancer when it undergoes mutation. items.title: Peruvian mummies raise questions about Wari conquest of Nasca civilization
items.summary: For centuries, historians have drawn the boundaries of where ancient people lived based on the evidence they left behind. items.title: The real cost of coal mines to people and planet
items.summary: The longer it takes to transition away from fossil fuels such as coal, the more costs accrue as climate change accelerates.

items.title: Ocean predator chemical cues could provide early warnings for toxic algal blooms
items.summary: A team of marine scientists led by researchers at the University of California, Santa Cruz, has developed a new approach to predicting harmful algal blooms (HABs), changing how oceanographers track these hazardous marine events.
